extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short speculative fiction to Strange Horizons
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for authors preparing and submitting short speculative-fiction stories to the online magazine Strange Horizons, including format, rights, payment, and editorial preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story doesn't have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it's probably not for us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred subject matter and perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Some particular things we love, or are interested in: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, settings, and cultures, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also welcome: unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives; stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification; hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other stories that explore and exploit the forms available to us (query first for format-specific submission guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to 10,000 words (under 5000 preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but consider up to 10,000; the longer the story, the less likely we are to be interested. Wordcount determined by the word-processor wordcount and rounded up to the next highest 100 words. Stories much over the limit cannot be considered; no minimum wordcount; short-shorts are acceptable. Serialized novels or novellas are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: File formats accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send only RTF, DOC or DOCX files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No email or postal submissions; use the Moksha submissions system upload form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted here, via our Moksha submissions system — no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to track stories correctly, we can only consider stories submitted through that form. If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, query immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous or multiple submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously are not allowed. If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English—we buy first English rights, including audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English. For translations, consider submitting to our sister magazine Samovar first; Samovar and Strange Horizons have independent submissions queues and different editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and re-publication window
rubrics_metrics.description: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights (including audio rights) for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After that period you are free to republish the story elsewhere. We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rate and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 10¢/word (USD), with a minimum payment of $60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is made within 60 days of contract; payment by check or PayPal according to the author's preference. Strange Horizons is considered a professional market by SFWA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter can be minimal: generally, these should be short and list just a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've got life experience relevant to your story, please mention it. Cover letters shouldn't include plot synopses or pitches. See sample cover letters page for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autoreply and response troubleshooting
rubrics_metrics.description: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately; missing an autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you and we may not be able to contact you when making a decision. If you don't get an email response to queries within a month, query again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don't withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future. If you need to withdraw, send an email telling us and explain why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To contact us for any reason, write to fiction@strangehorizons.com with the word QUERY: at the beginning of your subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a few words to the subject line to indicate what you're querying about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content allowances (language, sex, violence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Things which are fine: Profanity is fine. Use whatever words are appropriate for your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore. British spellings are fine. We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content exclusions and unacceptable submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Things we won't consider: Stories above 10,000 words; partial or incomplete stories; unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English; stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons; multiple stories at once from the same author; poetry or nonfiction (wrong department).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please don't send part of a story and ask us to request the rest later. Submissions previously sent to Strange Horizons—even if revised—will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of translations and sister magazine
rubrics_metrics.description: Special note on translations: our quarterly sister magazine Samovar specializes in translations: we encourage you to submit all translations there first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samovar and Strange Horizons have independent submissions queues and different editors; submissions to either magazine are only read for that magazine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental formats procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypertext fiction, interactive fiction, and other experimental forms are welcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a work of this type that you think might be a good fit for Strange Horizons, please query us to discuss how to submit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission metadata and manuscript presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible. Along with your name and contact information in the upper left, you may also add your pronouns (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your legal name does not need to be anywhere on your submission; legal name will only be requested if story is accepted for contract and payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous/multiple submission consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously are disallowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple stories at once from the same author are also not accepted. Violations can lead to rejection and/or being barred from consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational/seasonal submission windows
rubrics_metrics.description: We are currently closed to submissions; we will reopen to submissions for 48 hours on January 19th 2026 at 3 p.m. UTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check top of page to see if open before attempting to submit. Everything else on the page is intended to clarify or expand the above rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and market recognition detail
rubrics_metrics.description: SFWA officially considers Strange Horizons a professional market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of professional rates and market recognition details are provided for authors to assess professional status.
